D-bear-drive-0008.name: By Goatskin Creek
D-bear-drive-0008.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
D-bear-drive-0008.parkWhat: pull off on Arthurs 100 FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2011 (15 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2021 (fire N62459), 350 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Goatskin Creek 50 m W: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 8-14, Region 8. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.

evidence.t: Road: Rendell 8000, 6.7 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS).
4 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
9 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).
